body: Jet Airways suspended all flights on 17 Apr 2019 after lenders refused ~Rs 400 cr emergency funding; Indian Oil had stopped fuel on 5 Apr. Net debt ~$1.2 bn; fleet fell from 123 to 41 planes by Mar 2019. The airline posted losses in 8 of the 10 years to 2019; domestic share fell from ~22.5% (2015) to ~15.5% (2018). Etihad bought 24% for $379 m in 2013 -- a rescue mistaken by many as validation. The stock (IPO 2005 at Rs 1,100; peaked >Rs 1,000 in 2006 and again ~Rs 900 in Jan 2018) slid to ~Rs 30s after grounding; a Jalan-Kalrock revival failed and the Supreme Court ordered liquidation in Nov 2024. Visible flags: (1) negative net worth for years; (2) the overpriced 2007 Sahara (JetLite) acquisition; (3) sale-and-leaseback gains propping profits; (4) Aug 2018: the board deferred Q1 results and salaries were delayed; (5) aircraft lessors grounding planes for non-payment (late 2018); (6) promoter Naresh Goyal refusing to cede control. Lesson: in airlines, cumulative losses + negative equity + delayed results/salaries means equity is an option on a bailout; a strategic investor's entry is not a safety net. Speculative rallies in grounded/insolvent stocks are noise, not recovery.

data.early_signals: losses 8/10 yrs; negative net worth; delayed results Aug 2018; salary delays; lessor groundings
data.lesson: Negative equity + delayed results = disqualifier in airlines
data.spotted_by: lessors and oil marketing companies (stopped credit)

title: Jet Airways grounding (Apr 2019) and liquidation
